rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-01-01 (ch1 number-normalized dup of k2, both 'find the slope of the line through (#,#) and (#,#).'): true unintentional duplicate, not spaced practice -- the challenge step repeated the mid-lesson check's bare two-point computation verbatim. Rewrote ch1 into a rate-in-context transfer item (hiking trail, meters/minutes) holding the same points and answer (3); commonErrors, fallbackFeedback, explanationVariants and hints recomputed for the new framing (12-3=9, 5-2=3, 9/3=3 reverified). Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[] (was [ch1]).
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in lf-01-01 again normalizes (digits->#) equal to another step in the same lesson, or ch1's recomputed arithmetic (9,-3 traps; answer 3) is found wrong.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-01-03 (k2 number-normalized dup of k1, both slopeTriangle 'build the triangle for the line through A (#,#) and B (#,#).'): legitimate spaced practice, not a duplicate. k1's points force a FALLING/negative-slope triangle (right after c1/i1 teach sign-from-direction); k2's points force a RISING/positive-slope triangle (right after c2/i2 teach the zero/horizontal case) -- same construction action under an opposite sign constraint, immediately followed by k3's four-way sign sort. The constraint (resulting sign) differs even though the text template does not; this is the lesson's own core discrimination skill, not an accidental re-ask. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines k1/k2 must also differ in wording/representation (not just numeric sign outcome), or that sign alone is not a sufficient constraint differentiator for this workstream.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-02-01 (i3 number-normalized dup of k2, both 'for y = #x + #, find y when x = #.'): legitimate interleaved spaced practice. k2 is the first evaluate-at-a-point rep, built with the scaffolded exactNumberLab/approximationEvaluate widget (explore constants m/c/x through an approxFormula) right after c2 teaches the x=0 substitution mechanic; i2/k3 then interleave two identification tasks; i3 re-tests the same evaluate skill unscaffolded (plain numeric widget, different action/mechanic) as spaced retrieval immediately before ch1's harder subtraction-based evaluate challenge. Different interaction mechanic plus deliberate interleaving, not an accidental re-ask. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines exactNumberLab vs plain numeric is not a sufficient action differentiator, or that the interleaving gap (i2,k3) is too coincidental to count as deliberate spacing.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-03-01 (k3, ch1 number-normalized dups of i2, all buildExpression 'build the point-slope equation for the line through (#,#) with slope #.'): legitimate escalating-constraint practice. i2 = 0 negatives (baseline mechanics); k3 = 1 negative (point's y-coordinate, exercising c3's hidden-negative reading, single distinct trap on the y sign); ch1 = 2 negatives (point's x-coordinate AND the slope, its own body says 'Two negatives to handle', two distinct traps on x sign and slope sign). Same build action, deliberately escalating constraint and distinct named misconception traps at each step. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines the 0/1/2-negative escalation is not a sufficient constraint differentiator for this workstream, or that i2/k3/ch1 must also differ in wording.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-03-02 (ch1 number-normalized dup of k3, both 'convert y - # = #(x - #) to slope-intercept form. what is b?'): legitimate escalating-constraint practice. k1 baseline w/ reminder; k2 tests a hidden-negative point coordinate (y+4 => y1=-4); k3 (after i3 teaches the backward direction) is a plain positive reinforcement of the forward conversion; ch1 ('Negative slope, full convert') tests a negative SLOPE, a distinct sign-error source from k2 with its own two traps on subtracting a negative slope term. Different constraint (source of the sign complication) at each step, escalating to the hardest case. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines negative-point-coordinate vs negative-slope is not a sufficient constraint differentiator, or that k3 must also differ from k1/k2/ch1 in wording.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-03-03 (k2 number-normalized dup of k1, both 'find the x-intercept of #x+#y=# (set y=#).'): true unintentional duplicate AND a content mismatch -- c2 teaches both intercepts, i2 tests y-intercept of the k1 equation, but k2 then re-tested x-intercept of a new equation instead of the y-intercept i2 had just taught, leaving y-intercept graded nowhere. Rewrote k2 to test the y-intercept of the same new equation (4x+5y=20 crosses the y-axis at y=4, cross-verified against the old k2's own trap feedback which already stated 20/5=4) in wording distinct from i2's ('Where does 4x+5y=20 cross the y-axis? (Set x=0.)' vs i2's 'Find the y-intercept of...'); traps/approxConstants/approxFormula swapped from x-intercept (A,C/A) to y-intercept (B,C/B). Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[] (was [k2]), and new k2 template does not collide with i2's either.
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in lf-03-03 again normalizes equal to another step, or the y-intercept arithmetic (5y=20 => y=4; traps 5 and 20) is found wrong.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-04-01 (k2, ch1 number-normalized dups of i2, all 'a line passes through (#,#) with slope #. what is b?'): legitimate escalating-constraint practice, same pattern as lf-03-01/lf-03-02 in this course. i2 = one negative (slope -1, point positive), answer 7; k2 = one negative (point x=-1, slope positive), answer 5; ch1 = two negatives (point x=-2 AND slope -3, body says 'Two negatives to manage'), answer -4. Each step's traps are freshly computed for its own sign combination (mis-signing y1 / adding instead of subtracting / mishandling negative-times-negative). No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines this recurring escalating-negative pattern is not a sufficient constraint differentiator across the course, or that i2/k2/ch1 must also differ in wording.

rationale: PROGRESSION-lf-04-02 (k3, ch1 number-normalized dups of k1, all 'the line through (#,#) and (#,#) has slope #. find b.'): mixed disposition. k3 was a true unintentional duplicate (all-positive, no differentiation from k1) -- rewrote to a negative-slope case in different wording ('A line's slope is -2, and it runs through (1,8) and (4,2). What is b?', answer 10; slope check (2-8)/(4-1)=-2 confirmed, b cross-verified via both points, traps 8/6 recomputed). ch1 was left as-is: its body already says 'Negatives in a point' (negative point x-coordinate), the lesson's genuine escalation from k1's all-positive baseline, matching the accepted escalating-constraint pattern already used in lf-03-01/lf-03-02/lf-04-01 in this same course; now distinct from k3 too. Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[ch1] only (was [k3,ch1]), retained by design.
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in lf-04-02 again normalizes equal to another step besides the accepted k1/ch1 sign-escalation pair, or k3's recomputed arithmetic (slope -2, b=10, traps 8/6) is found wrong.

rationale: PROGRESSION-rns-01-01 (ch1 number-normalized dup of k4, both '# as a decimal is:' -- the fraction n/d collapses to one # token under the detector's own regex): legitimate escalation, not a duplicate. k4 = 9/20 = 0.45, a straightforward terminating case. ch1 ('A trickier one') = 5/11 = 0.4545..., a repeating-block case whose distractors target a different misconception cluster (assuming it stops after 2 digits, naming the wrong repeating block '4' instead of '45'). Different classification outcome and different misconception target. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines terminate-vs-repeat classification is not a sufficient misconception differentiator, or that k4/ch1 must also differ in prompt wording.

rationale: PROGRESSION-rns-01-02 (k2 number-normalized dup of k1, both '# will:' since the fraction collapses to one # token): true unintentional duplicate. k1 (1/12=2^2x3) and old k2 (5/6=2x3) had identical reasoning (leftover 3), identical outcome (repeats), near-identical distractors -- both used the same stray prime 3, risking the narrow misconception 'numbers with a 3 don't terminate.' Rewrote k2 to 5/14 (14=2x7, repeats), generalizing the rule to a different stray prime (7) in reworded text ('5/14 - terminate or repeat? (14 = 2 x 7)'); distractor structure rebuilt in parallel with recomputed numbers. Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[] (was [k2]); arithmetic reverified 5/14=0.357142857142... repeating since 7 is not 2 or 5.
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in rns-01-02 again normalizes equal to another step, or the 5/14 classification/distractor feedback is found wrong.

rationale: PROGRESSION-rns-01-03 (i2 dup of k1 both '#... equals:'; k3 dup of k2 both '#... (block "#" repeats) equals:'): mixed disposition. i2 kept -- k1 uses answerMode fraction (free-entry) vs i2's answerMode choice (mcq recognition against named-misconception distractors), i2's own body 'One more single-digit conversion' signals deliberate spaced reinforcement; different interaction mechanic. k3 rewritten -- old k3 (0.181818...=2/11) and k2 (0.454545...=5/11, also c2's own worked example) were a true duplicate, same fraction-entry two-digit-block task, both reducible by 9, no differentiation. Redesigned k3 to 0.131313...=13/99, verified already in lowest terms (gcd(13,99)=1 via Euclidean algorithm), a genuinely new misconception target (don't over-simplify) in reworded text; fractionErrors recomputed (13/100 terminating trap kept, new 13/9 single-digit-denominator-confusion trap added). Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[i2] only (was [i2,k3]).
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in rns-01-03 again normalizes equal to another step besides the accepted k1/i2 pair, or the 13/99 already-reduced claim or its traps are found wrong.

rationale: PROGRESSION-rns-02-01 (i3, k3 number-normalized dups of k2, all rootClassify '#... is:'... wait '√# is:'): legitimate rehearsal-then-assessment. k2 = classify sqrt50 (irrational). i3 (interactive, ungraded) immediately follows with the contrasting case sqrt100 (rational, perfect square 10^2) as practice. k3 (the very next step, graded check) checks that identical rational/perfect-square skill with sqrt81=9 -- i3 directly rehearses what k3 then grades, unlike the rns-01-02/rns-01-03 collisions above which had unrelated material between the colliding pair. Classification contrast with k2 plus direct practice-before-check adjacency. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines direct interactive-then-check adjacency on the identical job is not a sufficient differentiator, or that i3/k3 must also differ in wording/task type.

rationale: PROGRESSION-rns-02-03 (k2, ch1 number-normalized dups of k1, all rootBracket '#^2 = # and #^2 = #. so sqrt# is between:'): legitimate escalation. k1 brackets sqrt2 to tenths (1.4-1.5). k2 (body: 'Narrow it further') brackets the SAME sqrt2 to hundredths (1.41-1.42), a deliberate precision escalation. ch1 (body: 'Apply the narrowing idea to a new number') brackets a DIFFERENT radicand, sqrt10, at hundredths -- an explicit transfer task. Precision escalation then transfer to a new target, both allowed differentiators. No content edit made.
reopenCondition: An assessor determines precision-escalation-on-the-same-radicand or transfer-to-a-new-radicand are not sufficient differentiators for this workstream.

rationale: Two rows closed. PROGRESSION-rns-03-01 (k2, ch1 number-normalized dups of k1, all 'between which two whole numbers does sqrt# lie? type the smaller one.'): ch1 kept (brackets sqrt150, hints explicitly extend the perfect-square list to 169, genuine recall-range escalation). k2 rewritten -- true duplicate of k1 (same recall range, no differentiation) -- now asks for the LARGER bound of sqrt95 instead of the smaller (answer 10, was 9; 81<95<100 verified), a real action change guarding the 'always report the smaller bound' shortcut; traps recomputed (9 as wrong-direction trap, 11 as one-square-too-far). Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[ch1] only. CROSS-FIX: CHOICE-0056 (k3, lone-justification leak) -- correct option alone carried 'since...' reasoning while option b was bare '9'. Gave all four options parallel verdict+reason structure (b: 'since 9 is the smaller of the two bounds'; c reworded to 'since that's the number exactly between 9 and 10' with feedback correspondingly rewritten; d: 'since 95 seems close to both 81 and 100'), ids/order/correct flags/evaluator semantics unchanged, all labels now 40-55 chars (no length tell). Every distractor's stated premise verified factually true (9 is the smaller bound; 9.5 is the midpoint of 9,10) with only its conclusion wrong.
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in rns-03-01 again normalizes equal to another step besides the accepted k1/ch1 pair, k3's new distractor reasoning is found mathematically false, or a lone-justification asymmetry reappears among k3's options.

rationale: PROGRESSION-rns-03-02 (i2,k2,k3,ch1 number-normalized dups of k1, all 'to one decimal place, sqrt# ~ ____', widest cluster in this batch): mixed disposition, adjudicated per instance. i2 kept (canonical sqrt2, ungraded rehearsal). k3/ch1 kept (genuine bracket-size escalation to 5-6 then 9-10 whole-number bounds; ch1 hints re-walk the full bracket-then-narrow process as capstone). k2 rewritten -- true duplicate (same 1-2 bracket as i2, zero escalation, 4th identical instance). Redesigned to a close-call case: sqrt6 rounds to 2.4 by the narrowest possible margin (2.4^2=5.76, gap 0.24; 2.5^2=6.25, gap 0.25; 0.24<0.25 verified), a genuinely new constraint (naive rounding intuition unreliable) in reworded text. Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[i2,k3,ch1] (was [i2,k2,k3,ch1]).
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in rns-03-02 again normalizes equal to another step besides the accepted k1/i2/k3/ch1 set, or the sqrt6 close-call arithmetic (0.24 vs 0.25) is found wrong.

rationale: PROGRESSION-alg1-01-01 (ch1 number-normalized dup of k1, both 'solve for x: #x + # = #'): true unintentional duplicate -- k1 (4x+8=28) and old ch1 (5x+3=38) were both baseline all-positive two-step solves with zero escalation; k2 already owns the negative-constant case and k3 the procedural question. Rewrote ch1 to the untested negative-coefficient case: 'What value of x makes -3x + 4 = 19 true?', answer -5 (19-4=15, 15/-3=-5; check -3*-5+4=19). Traps recomputed: 15 (bare -3x) and 5 (sign-drop dividing by -3 as if +3). Detector re-run: number-normalized-prompts=[] (was [ch1]).
reopenCondition: Any widget-bearing step in alg1-01-01 again normalizes equal to another step, or the -3x+4=19 arithmetic/traps are found wrong.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 and ch1 both number-normalized to k1's exact template "solve for x: #x + # = #x + #", and k2's numbers (7x+3=4x+15) were literally c2's own worked example replayed as the graded check, giving zero transfer. Rewrote k2 to 6x-4=2x+20 (x=6), introducing a negative left-side constant (literal "-" not adjacent to a digit keeps the template textually distinct: "...#x - # = #x + #"). Rewrote ch1 to 3x+4=7x+20 (x=-4), reversing which side carries the bigger coefficient (tests transfer of c2's "subtract the smaller x-term" rule when that term sits on the left instead of the right) and yielding a negative solution for the first time in the lesson; reworded the stem to "What is x, given ...?" so the template itself (not just the numbers) differs from k1/k2. All commonErrors/hints/explanationVariants recomputed and verified by hand (6*6-4=2*6+20=32; 3*(-4)+4=7*(-4)+20=-8). k1 kept as anchor (baseline, all-positive). No CHOICE_SURFACE_INTEGRITY row for this lesson.
reopenCondition: If k1, the new k2, or the new ch1 prompt text is edited such that two of the three normalize to the same template again, or if the recomputed arithmetic in k2/ch1 (answers, commonErrors, hints, explanationVariants) is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: only ch1 flagged, number-normalized to k1's template "solve for x: x/# + # = #" — same all-positive division-then-add-constant shape as k1, same final answer (15) as k1 even, and weaker than k2 (which already covers a negative constant) despite being the capstone challenge. Rewrote ch1 to "9 + x/4 = 3" (x=-24): flips the constant to lead the equation (order shift, changes the literal token order so the template itself differs: "# + x/# = #") and drives both the intermediate (x/4=-6) and final answer negative for the first time in this lesson -- a genuine escalation beyond k1 and k2, appropriate for the challenge tier. k1 and k2 kept as-is (k1 is the anchor; k2 already had its own negative-constant differentiation and was never flagged). Verified: 9+(-24)/4=9-6=3.
reopenCondition: If k1 or the new ch1 prompt text is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic (answer, commonErrors) is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 and ch1 both number-normalized to k1's exact template "solve for x: x/# + x/# = #" -- all three were plain two-fraction LCD-clear sums differing only in which coprime denominator pair was used, and k1's numbers were literally c1's own worked example replayed. Rewrote k2 to "x/3 + x/9 + 2 = 10" (x=18): adds a third, bare-constant term alongside the two fractions (new template "...x/# + x/# + # = #") and uses a non-coprime denominator pair (9 is a multiple of 3, so LCD=9, not 27) -- tests both the taught-but-unassessed misconception of forgetting to scale a bare addend by the LCD (distinct from k1/c2's already-covered 'forgot to scale the other SIDE' case) and the 'LCD is not just the product' idea already modeled in i2. Rewrote ch1 to "x/2 - x/8 = 6" (x=16): a subtraction between the two fraction terms (new template "...x/# - x/# = #"), also a non-coprime pair (8 is a multiple of 2). k1 kept as anchor; k3 (MCQ, untouched) was never flagged. All arithmetic recomputed and verified by hand (3*18+18+18=90 confirms 4x=72,x=18; 4*16-16=48 confirms 3x=48,x=16).
reopenCondition: If k1, or the new k2/ch1 prompt text, is edited such that two of the three normalize to the same template again, or if the recomputed arithmetic is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 and ch1 both number-normalized to k1's template "solve for x: #x + # = #" (decimal points are absorbed into the number token same as any digit, so one-decimal-place vs whole-number distinctions are invisible to the detector) -- all three were also keyed to the identical final answer x=5, the clearest signal of pure copy-and-reskin. Rewrote k2 to "1.5 + 0.25x = 3" (x=6): order-flipped (constant leads, template becomes "# + #x = #") AND escalates to two decimal places, requiring recognition that ×100 (not the ×10 used everywhere else in the lesson) is needed to clear -- a genuinely new constraint. Rewrote ch1 to "0.6x - 0.9 = 1.5" (x=4): a subtraction (template "#x - # = #", the literal '-' is space-separated from the digit so it is not absorbed into the number token) -- new sign-handling demand for the capstone. k1 kept as anchor; k3 (MCQ) was never flagged. Arithmetic recomputed and verified (150+25*6=300; 6*4-9=15).
reopenCondition: If k1, or the new k2/ch1 prompt text, is edited such that two of the three normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k3 number-normalized to k1's template "using f = #c/# + #, find f when c = #." -- both were plug-into-the-already-solved-formula evaluations at a positive C, differing only in the numeric input (100 vs 25); ch1 (unflagged) already legitimately escalates by requiring the student to rearrange the ORIGINAL unsolved formula before evaluating, so k3 needed its own distinct job. Rewrote k3 to "What is F when C = -40, using F = 9C/5 + 32?" (F=-40): reworded the stem (clause order flipped, changing the literal template) and moved to a negative input for the first time in the lesson, landing on the well-known -40 degree crossover point where Fahrenheit and Celsius coincide (a genuine sign-handling escalation plus a memorable pedagogical hook, distinct from k1's positive case and from ch1's rearrange-then-evaluate task). k1 and ch1 unchanged (k1 is the anchor; ch1 was never flagged). Arithmetic verified: 9*(-40)/5+32 = -72+32 = -40; commonErrors -72 (forgot +32) and -8 (added 32 to C directly, skipped scaling) recomputed for the new input.
reopenCondition: If k1 or the new k3 prompt text is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic (F=-40, commonErrors -72/-8) is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: ch1 number-normalized to k1's template "evaluate #^# · #^#." -- both were plain numeric base-2 product-rule evaluations differing only in the exponents, with ch1 (the capstone) offering no escalation over k1 despite k2 (quotient) and k3 (variable quotient) already existing between them. Rewrote ch1 to "Evaluate (2^5 · 2^2) / 2^3." (=16): a genuine synthesis task requiring BOTH rules taught in this lesson in sequence (product rule then quotient rule), appropriate for a capstone -- new template "evaluate (#^# · #^#) / #^#.", textually and structurally distinct from k1. k1/k2/k3/i1/i2/i3 unchanged (k1 is the anchor; nothing else was flagged). Verified: 2^5*2^2/2^3 = 32*4/8 = 16.
reopenCondition: If k1 or the new ch1 prompt text is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic (16, and commonErrors 1024/128) is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 number-normalized to i3's template "simplify (x^#)^# to x^?. what is the exponent?" (both plain single-variable power-of-power fill-ins), and ch1 number-normalized to k1's template "evaluate (#^#)^#." (both plain numeric power-of-power evaluations). Rewrote k2 to "Simplify (x^4 y^2)^3 to x^a y^b. What is the exponent on y?" (=6): tests the TWO-VARIABLE / several-factors case that c3 explicitly teaches but which no prior check item actually assessed (i3 and original-k2 were both single-variable) -- new template with an extra y-token and a 'which variable' framing, and a new distractor misconception (reporting the OTHER variable's exponent, 12 instead of 6). Rewrote ch1 to "Evaluate (2^2 · 3)^2." (=144): synthesizes the lesson's two threads (power-of-a-power AND power-of-a-product, taught in c1/c2 but never jointly assessed numerically) -- the outer square must hit both the already-squared 2^2 and the bare 3, a genuine capstone-level demand. k1 and i3 kept unchanged as anchors; k3 (MCQ) was never flagged. Arithmetic verified: (x^4 y^2)^3 -> exponent on y = 2*3=6, on x = 4*3=12; (2^2*3)^2 = 12^2 = 144.
reopenCondition: If i3/k1, or the new k2/ch1 prompt text, is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k3 (mcq) number-normalized to i2's template "what is #^# as a fraction?" (both plain numeric-base negative-exponent-to-fraction MCQs), and ch1 number-normalized to k1's template "simplify #^# · #^# to #^?. what is the exponent?" (both numeric-base products landing on a negative exponent). Rewrote k3 to "What is x^-4 as a fraction?": moves the reciprocal-conversion skill to a VARIABLE base for the first time (i2 and the original k3 were both numeric bases 2/3) -- new template "what is x^# as a fraction?", with distractors adapted to variable algebra (-x^4 = made it negative not reciprocal; x^4 = dropped the negative without reciprocating). Rewrote ch1 to "Simplify 2^-3 / 2^2 to 2^?. What is the exponent?" (=-5): switches from the product rule (already covered by k1 numerically and k2 with a variable base) to the QUOTIENT rule landing on a negative result -- new template using '/' instead of '·', and a genuinely new demand (subtracting exponents where the FIRST one is already negative, not just the second). i2/k1/k2 unchanged as anchors. Arithmetic verified: -3-2=-5.
reopenCondition: If i2/k1, or the new k3/ch1 prompt text, is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 number-normalized to k1's template "subtract: (#x^# + #x - #) - (#x^# + #x - #). what is the coefficient of x?" -- both plain-structure polynomial subtractions asking for the x-coefficient, differing only in numbers (k2's job of illustrating a column CANCELLING to zero is a nice idea but was carried entirely by the numbers, invisible to the text-based detector). Rewrote k2 to ask for the coefficient of x^2 instead of x, on a new polynomial pair (4x^2+5x-3)-(4x^2-x+3) where the LEADING (x^2) column is what cancels (4-4=0) -- new template ending "...coefficient of x^#?" instead of "...coefficient of x?", plus the second polynomial now uses an implicit-coefficient middle term ("- x" not "+ #x"), a second independent textual differentiator. This preserves k2's original 'a column can cancel to zero' pedagogical purpose while generalizing it (not just the x-column can vanish) and keeps distinct column coverage across the lesson (k1=x-column negative result, k2=x^2-column cancels, k3=constant column, ch1=x-column sign-flip). Updated the variant form tag from subX to subX2 to match. k1/k3/ch1/i1/i2/i3 unchanged -- k1 is the anchor, nothing else was flagged.
reopenCondition: If k1 or the new k2 prompt text is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic (x^2-coefficient 0, commonErrors 8/4) is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 number-normalized to i3's template "multiply (#x^#)(x^# + #x - #). what is the coefficient of x^#?" -- both used the literally IDENTICAL polynomial multiplication (4x^2)(x^2+2x-1), differing only in which power's coefficient was asked (x^3 vs x^4), and that digit is stripped by the detector same as any other, so the two prompts normalized identically. Rewrote k2 to a fresh multiplication, "Multiply (5x^2)(x^2 - 3x + 2). What is the coefficient of x^4?" (=5): new numbers AND a flipped sign pattern (negative middle term, positive constant, vs i3's positive-middle/negative-constant) -- new template "...(x^# - #x + #)...", textually distinct, while preserving k2's original 'leading/top term' role (distinct from i3's x^3-column role). i1/i2/i3/k1/k3/ch1 unchanged -- i3 is the anchor, nothing else was flagged. Arithmetic verified: 5*1=5 (x^4 coefficient), 5*(-3)=-15 (x^3 coefficient, used as a commonError distractor).
reopenCondition: If i3 or the new k2 prompt text is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic (5, commonErrors 1/-15) is found inconsistent.

rationale: (b) true duplicate: k2 number-normalized to i2's template "factor (x^# - #)." (both plain x^2-minus-constant difference-of-squares prompts, though k2's buildExpression widget already made its ACTION genuinely different from i2's mcq -- only the literal prompt text collided), and ch1 number-normalized to k3's template "factor (#x^# - #)." (both coefficient-squared-x^2-minus-constant, buildExpression, differing only in which number went where). Rewrote k2's prompt to "Build the factored form of x^2 - 49." (kept the buildExpression action and target-shape, changed the target number 25->49 to stop double-covering k1's own 25 fact, and reworded the stem so the template itself now differs: "build the factored form of x^# - #."). Rewrote ch1 to "Factor (36x^2 - 25y^2)." =(6x+5y)(6x-5y): introduces a SECOND variable for the first time in the lesson (every prior item was a single variable squared minus a plain constant, or a coefficient-squared single variable minus a constant) -- a genuine transfer of the a^2-b^2 pattern to two-variable expressions, appropriate for the capstone; new template with an extra "y^#" token. i1/k1/i3/k3 unchanged -- i2/k3 are the anchors, k1/i3 were never flagged. Arithmetic verified: (6x+5y)(6x-5y) expands to 36x^2-25y^2 with the middle terms (30xy-30xy) cancelling.
reopenCondition: If i2/k3, or the new k2/ch1 prompt text, is edited such that they normalize to the same template again, or the recomputed arithmetic is found inconsistent.
